reason: The cited evidence (E2) shows that Ti addition and TiC precipitates can increase strength in CoCrFeNiTix alloys, but it does not support the premise that the equimolar alloy is a nearly random single-phase FCC solid solution with only moderate lattice distortion and few obstacles; in fact, E2 indicates TiC formation already occurs during standard processing, contradicting the baseline description. E1 is about Nb additions and SPS processing in CoCrFeNi, providing no direct support for the key premises regarding Ti or the proposed intervention.
premises: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi forms a nearly random single-phase FCC solid solution with only moderate lattice distortion.
Limited solid-solution strengthening arises from this homogeneous distribution, providing few obstacles to dislocation glide.
A controlled heat treatment with minor carbon addition or thermo-mechanical processing can induce Ti-rich precipitates (e.g., TiC) or short-range chemical ordering.
Such precipitates or ordered domains act as effective dislocation pinning centers, increasing strength and hardness.
The baseline single-phase FCC state exhibits lower hardness and strength with excellent ductility compared to the treated state.
